title: Reduction of G-equivariant cosheaves to a QFD
body_html:
Reduction of $G$-equivariant cosheaves to a QFD

Setting: $S \subseteq X$ is a [[quasi-fundamental domain|node:equivariant_sheaves.quasi_fundamental_domain]] for the $G$-action with distinguished subgroup $G' \le G$; $\mathscr C$ is a category (with enough structure to house cosheaves — the abstract poset framework demands only Category C). The proposition unfolds $G$-equivariant cosheaves on $X$ into $G'$-equivariant cosheaves on $S$ carrying additional stabiliser-action data.

The K-cosheaf of subgroups

The "additional data" on $S$ is a K-cosheaf: a family $K = {K_E}_{E \in S}$ of subgroups of $G$ (not of $G'$!) satisfying three conditions.

Definition (K-cosheaf on a QFD). A K-cosheaf on $S$ is a map $K : X \to \mathrm{Subgroup}(G)$ (meaningful only on cells of $S$; extended arbitrarily elsewhere) with:

  • ($K$-mono) Cosheaf functoriality. For $E \preceq F$ in $S$, $K_F \le K_E$. (Same direction as $\Fix_G$: bigger cell, smaller subgroup.)
  • ($K$-eq) $G'$-equivariance. For $n \in G'$ and $E \in S$, $K_{n \cdot E} = n K_E n^{-1}$.
  • ($K$-fix) Fixator dominance. For every $E \in S$, $K_E \le \Stab_G(E)$.

The paper's fourth axiom, $K_E \cap G' \subseteq \Fix_{G'}(E)$, is a consequence of ($K$-fix): $k \in K_E \cap G' \Rightarrow k \in \Stab_G(E)$ (by fix) $\Rightarrow k \cdot E = E$, hence $k \in \Fix_{G'}(E) = G' \cap \Stab_G(E)$. No separate hypothesis is needed.

Relationship between $K$ and $P$

The K-cosheaf $K$ on $S$ (this node) and the induction cosheaf $P$ on $X'$ ([[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]]) have the same shape — both are functions cell $\to$ subgroup of $G$ — but their hypotheses differ in strength.

Hypothesis Induction ($P$) Reduction ($K$)
Cosheaf monotonicity ($P$0) $E \preceq F \Rightarrow P_F \le P_E$ ($K$-mono) $E \preceq F \Rightarrow K_F \le K_E$
$G'$-equivariance ($P$1) $nP_En^{-1} = P_{n \cdot E}$ ($K$-eq) $K_{n \cdot E} = nK_En^{-1}$
Stabiliser relation ($P$2) $P_E \cap G' \subseteq \Fix_{G'}(E)$ ($K$-fix) $K_E \le \Stab_G(E)$

The top two rows coincide. The third differs:

  • ($P$2) says "the part of $P_E$ lying in $G'$ fixes $E$" — weak.
  • ($K$-fix) says "every element of $K_E$ fixes $E$" — strong.

($K$-fix) $\Rightarrow$ ($P$2): for $m \in K_E \cap G'$, ($K$-fix) gives $m \cdot E = E$, so $m \in \Fix_{G'}(E) = G' \cap \Stab_G(E)$. The converse does not hold in general — a $P$-cosheaf can carry elements outside $G'$ that do not fix $E$, and such a $P$ is not a $K$.

Coincidence in the induced-space setting. When $X = G \times^P X'$ is the induced space of an `InductionDatum`, $\iota(X') \subseteq X$ is the sharp QFD (X' is a quasi-fundamental domain of the induced space), and the stabiliser formula (Cell-stabiliser and fixator formulas on the induced space Lemma A(2)) gives $P_E \subseteq \Stab_G(\iota E)$ — precisely ($K$-fix) on the image of $\iota$. In this case the induction cosheaf $P$ automatically upgrades to a K-cosheaf on $\iota(X')$, and the main compatibility hypothesis $\Stab_G(\iota E) = K_E \cdot \Fix_{G'}(E)$ becomes exactly Lemma A(1). The reduction proposition then specialises to a statement purely about $G \times^P X'$.

The converse — general K-cosheaves on a general QFD $S$ — is strictly more permissive: no assumption that $S$ arises from an induction is used.

The K-decomposed QFD orbit lemma

The bridge from the plain QFD orbit lemma (QFD orbit lemma: gE = hF iff there is n with nE=F and g⁻¹hn fixes E) to the K-cosheaf formalism requires one extra hypothesis on $K$ relative to the ambient stabiliser data:

Main compatibility hypothesis. For every $E \in S$, $$\Stab_G(E) = K_E \cdot \Fix_{G'}(E).$$ Equivalently: every $f \in \Stab_G(E)$ factors as $f = k \cdot m$ with $k \in K_E$ and $m \in \Fix_{G'}(E) = G' \cap \Stab_G(E)$.

Under this hypothesis, the plain QFD orbit lemma refines:

Lemma (K-decomposed QFD orbit lemma). For $E, F \in S$ and $g, h \in G$: $$ g \cdot E = h \cdot F \iff \exists\, n \in G',\; n \cdot E = F \wedge g^{-1} h n \in K_E. $$
proof_html:
($\Rightarrow$) By the plain QFD orbit lemma, $\exists n_0 \in G'$ with $n_0 E = F$ and $g^{-1} h n_0 \in \Stab_G(E)$. Apply the main compatibility hypothesis: $g^{-1} h n_0 = k \cdot m$ with $k \in K_E$ and $m \in \Fix_{G'}(E) = G' \cap \Stab_G(E)$. Set $n := n_0 m^{-1} \in G'$. Then $n \cdot E = n_0 m^{-1} \cdot E = n_0 \cdot E = F$ (since $m$ fixes $E$), and $g^{-1} h n = (k m) m^{-1} = k \in K_E$.

($\Leftarrow$) From $g^{-1} h n \in K_E \subseteq \Stab_G(E)$, $(g^{-1} h n) \cdot E = E$, so $g \cdot E = h n \cdot E = h \cdot F$. $\square$

A second useful form gives the K-decomposition of the "reachable-by-$G$" face relation on $S$:

Lemma (K-decomposed Hom-set for $]X/G[$). For $E, E' \in S$ and $g \in G$: $$ g \cdot E \preceq E' \iff \exists\, n, k \in G,\; n \in G',\; k \in K_E,\; n \cdot E \preceq E',\; g = n k. $$

Proof. Apply the K-decomposed orbit lemma to $g \cdot E = 1 \cdot (g \cdot E)$ with $F := g \cdot E$: extract $n \in G'$ with $n \cdot E = g \cdot E$ and $g^{-1} n \in K_E$; take $k := n^{-1} g$. The ($\Leftarrow$) direction uses ($K$-fix) directly. $\square$

The orbit category $]X/G[$ and the first equivalence

Definition (orbit category $]X/G[$). Objects: cells of $X$. Morphisms $E \to E'$: elements $g \in G$ with $g \cdot E \preceq E'$. Composition is group multiplication in reverse order.

Endomorphisms in $]X/G[$ are exactly the stabiliser: an endomorphism $g \in \Hom_{]X/G[}(E, E)$ has $g \cdot E \preceq E$, and dimension preservation ($G$-action is cellular) + strict monotonicity of $\dim$ on proper faces forces $g \cdot E = E$, so $g \in \Stab_G(E)$. This identification is a monoid isomorphism $\End_{]X/G[}(E) \cong \Stab_G(E)$.

The full subcategory on cells of $S \subseteq X$ is denoted $[S]_{]X/G[}$.

Proposition (first equivalence). If $S$ is a QFD for $G' \le G$, the inclusion functor $$ \iota : [S]_{]X/G[} \;\longrightarrow\; ]X/G[ $$ is an equivalence of categories.

Proof. Full-subcategory inclusions are always fully faithful. Essential surjectivity: any cell $E \in X$ has, by QFD surjectivity, a $g \in G$ and $F \in S$ with $g \cdot F = E$; then $g \in \Hom_{]X/G[}(F, E)$ and $g^{-1} \in \Hom_{]X/G[}(E, F)$ are mutually inverse isomorphisms. $\square$

Passing to functor categories: for any $\mathscr C$, $$ \underline{\mathrm{Fun}}([S]_{]X/G[}^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathscr C) \;\simeq\; \underline{\mathrm{Fun}}(]X/G[^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathscr C). $$

The reduction proposition

Combining the categorical equivalence with the K-cosheaf interpretation of the extra "action" data on the target side:

Proposition (reduction of equivariant cosheaves to a QFD). Let $K$ be a K-cosheaf on $S$ satisfying the main compatibility hypothesis $\Stab_G(E) = K_E \cdot \Fix_{G'}(E)$ for every $E \in S$. Then there are canonical equivalences of categories $$ \Cosh_G(X, \mathscr C) \;\simeq\; \underline{\mathrm{Fun}}([S]_{]X/G[}^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathscr C) \;\simeq\; \Cosh_{G', K}(S, \mathscr C), $$ where $\Cosh_{G', K}(S, \mathscr C)$ is the category of $G'$-equivariant cosheaves on $S$ valued in the subgroup-representation category $\mathrm{SRep}_G(\mathscr C)$, whose $E$-component $(V_E, a^{V_E})$ is a $K_E$-representation and whose morphism data intertwines the action of $\Stab_G(E) \cap K_E$ correctly.

Proof sketch.

  • First equivalence. Equivariant cosheaves on $X$ are functors $]X/G[^{\mathrm{op}} \to \mathscr C$ (with stalk action recorded on endomorphisms via the isomorphism $\End_{]X/G[}(E) \cong \Stab_G(E)$). Restricting along the inclusion $\iota : [S]_{]X/G[} \hookrightarrow ]X/G[$ — an equivalence by the first equivalence proposition — gives an equivalence of functor categories.

  • Second equivalence. Unpack the resulting functor $[S]_{]X/G[}^{\mathrm{op}} \to \mathscr C$ into $G'$-cosheaf data on $S$ (the poset-face part) together with a stabiliser action (the $\End(E) \cong \Stab_G(E)$ part). The stabiliser action factors through $K_E$ (via ($K$-fix): $K_E \le \Stab_G(E)$). Reconstruction uses the K-decomposed Hom-set: for $g : E \to E'$, canonically decompose $g = n k$ with $n \in G'$ and $k \in K_E$, then set $F(g) = a^{V_{E'}}_k \circ r^V_{n E, E'} \circ a^V_{n, E}$.

The two equivalences compose to give the full reduction. $\square$

Downstream

This proposition is the keystone for §4 (Heisenberg–Weil equivalence) and §8 (reduction to depth zero): equivariant data on the full generalised building $\BSigma$ can be checked on the apartment $A$. See Res and Sat functors between Coeff_G(B(Σ), Φ) and Coeff_M⁰(B(M)).

Lean formalization

The reduction is a large body of code split across five modules; the pieces are integrated but the outermost equivalence $\Cosh_G(X, \mathscr C) \simeq \Cosh_{G', K}(S, \mathscr C)$ is partially formalised — the categorical scaffolding (orbit category, QFD-driven functor-category equivalence, K-decomposed Hom-set lemma, $\mathrm{SRep}_G(\mathscr C)$ target category) is in place; the final identification of $\Cosh_G(X, \mathscr C)$ with $\mathrm{Fun}(]X/G[^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathscr C)$ is in progress in GCosheafToFun and its downstream files.

K-cosheaf data (SheafOnBuilding.KData)

structure KData (G' : Subgroup G) (S : Subcomplex X) where
  K : X → Subgroup G
  K_mono : ∀ ⦃E F : X⦄, E ≤ F → K F ≤ K E              -- (K-mono)
  K_equiv : ∀ (n : G') (E : X),
    K ((n : G) • E) = (K E).map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj n))  -- (K-eq)
  K_le_fix : ∀ (E : X), K E ≤ MulAction.stabilizer G E  -- (K-fix)

Derived lemmas: KData.smul_fix (k ∈ K_E → k • E = E) and KData.K1b (paper's (K1b) as a corollary).

K-decomposed QFD lemmas (SheafOnBuilding.IsQuasiFundDomain)

The two K-decomposed lemmas are the Lean-level statement of the paper's lem:qfd_surj_ext (orbit) and lem:qfd_equiv (Hom-set for $]X/G[$):

theorem orbit_iff_K
    (κ : KData G' S)
    (hFix : ∀ ⦃E : X⦄, E ∈ S → ∀ ⦃f : G⦄, f ∈ MulAction.stabilizer G E →
      ∃ (k m : G), k ∈ κ.K E ∧ m ∈ G' ∧
                   m ∈ MulAction.stabilizer G E ∧ f = k * m)
    {E F : X} (hE : E ∈ S) (hF : F ∈ S) (g h : G) :
    g • E = h • F ↔
      ∃ n ∈ G', n • E = F ∧ (g⁻¹ * h * n) ∈ κ.K E

theorem qfd_equiv_hom
    (κ : KData G' S) (hFix : ...)
    {E E' : X} (hE : E ∈ S) (hE' : E' ∈ S) (g : G) :
    g • E ≤ E' ↔
      ∃ (n k : G), n ∈ G' ∧ k ∈ κ.K E ∧ n • E ≤ E' ∧ g = n * k

The hFix hypothesis is exactly the paper's main compatibility hypothesis $\Stab_G(E) = K_E \cdot \Fix_{G'}(E)$, phrased as an existential factorisation. It stays as a hypothesis rather than becoming a KData field — the K-cosheaf data itself does not depend on the ambient QFD's stabiliser structure.

Orbit category (SheafOnBuilding.OrbitCat)

abbrev OrbitCat (G X : Type*) : Type _ := X
def Mor (E E' : OrbitCat G X) : Type _ :=
  {g : G // g • (E : X) ≤ (E' : X)}
scoped instance category : Category (OrbitCat G X) where
  Hom E E' := Mor E E'
  id  := Mor.id
  comp := Mor.comp
  ...

OrbitCat G X is an abbrev for X so MulAction, PartialOrder, AbstractCellComplex are visible without coercion; the Category instance is scoped to avoid clashing with X's built-in Preorder-derived category.

Endomorphism identification:

def endMorEquivStabilizer (E : OrbitCat G X) :
    Mor E E ≃ MulAction.stabilizer G (E : X)          -- Equiv
def endMulEquivStabilizer (E : OrbitCat G X) :
    End E ≃* MulAction.stabilizer G (E : X)           -- MulEquiv
def endToStabilizer (E : OrbitCat G X) :
    End E →* MulAction.stabilizer G (E : X)           -- MonoidHom

The ≃* upgrade uses CategoryTheory.End's convention $x * y = y \circ x$, matching subgroup multiplication.

First equivalence (SheafOnBuilding.OrbitCat.OnSubcomplex)

abbrev OnSubcomplex (S : Subcomplex X) :=
  ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun E => (E : X) ∈ S)
abbrev ιOnSubcomplex (S : Subcomplex X) :
    OnSubcomplex S ⥤ OrbitCat G X := ObjectProperty.ι _

theorem ιOnSubcomplex_essSurj (G' : Subgroup G) (S : Subcomplex X)
    [IsQuasiFundDomain G' S] : (ιOnSubcomplex S).EssSurj

theorem ιOnSubcomplex_isEquivalence (G' : Subgroup G) (S : Subcomplex X)
    [IsQuasiFundDomain G' S] : (ιOnSubcomplex S).IsEquivalence

ess_surj uses IsQuasiFundDomain.surj: any $E : ]X/G[$ receives a $g \cdot F = E$ with $F \in S$, and then $g$ and $g^{-1}$ are mutually inverse morphisms in $]X/G[$. Fully-faithful is automatic for full- subcategory inclusions. Combined via CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence.mk.

Functor-category equivalence (SheafOnBuilding.OrbitFunEquiv)

noncomputable def funCatEquivOfQFD (G' : Subgroup G) (S : Subcomplex X)
    [IsQuasiFundDomain G' S] :
    ((OnSubcomplex S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C) ≌ ((OrbitCat G X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C) :=
  letI := ιOnSubcomplex_isEquivalence G' S
  Equivalence.congrLeft (Functor.asEquivalence (ιOnSubcomplex S).op)

This is the categorical form of the paper's "first equivalence" $\underline{\mathrm{Fun}}([S]_{]X/G[}^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathscr C) \simeq \underline{\mathrm{Fun}}(]X/G[^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathscr C)$.

Target category $\mathrm{SRep}_G(\mathscr C)$ (SheafOnBuilding.SRep)

structure SRep where
  K : Subgroup G
  V : C
  ρ : K →* Aut V

@[ext]
structure SRep.Hom (X Y : SRep G C) where
  f : X.K →* Y.K
  ...  -- injectivity of f + intertwining condition

Standalone — no cell-complex machinery required.

Cosh ↦ functor on $]X/G[^{\mathrm{op}}$ (in progress:

SheafOnBuilding.GCosheafToFun)

Building block for the functor $\Cosh_G(X, \mathscr C) \to \underline{\mathrm{Fun}}(]X/G[^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathscr C)$:

noncomputable def GCosheaf.mapOfG
    (W : GCosheaf G X C) {E E' : X} (g : G) (hg : g • E' ≤ E) :
    W.base.obj (op E) ⟶ W.base.obj (op E') :=
  W.base.map (homOfLE hg).op ≫ (W.equiv.act g E').inv

theorem GCosheaf.mapOfG_one (W : GCosheaf G X C) (E : X) :
    W.mapOfG (1 : G) ... = 𝟙 (W.base.obj (op E))

The full functor and its inverse (the second equivalence of the proposition) are not yet packaged; the Basic.lean file header notes this as "pending". Once complete, composing with funCatEquivOfQFD delivers the full reduction $\Cosh_G(X, \mathscr C) \simeq \Cosh_{G', K}(S, \mathscr C)$ as a chain of category equivalences.

K↔P bridge (not yet in Lean)

Neither direction of the correspondence between KData and InductionDatum is formalised:

  • InductionDatum → KData (specialisation direction). Given d : InductionDatum X', the pair $(\iota(X'), \mathrm{Subcomplex.ofIota}\ d)$ is a QFD of $\mathrm{InducedSpace}\ d$ (via isQuasiFundDomain_subcomplexOfIota), and $P$ satisfies ($K$-fix) on $\iota(X')$ (via P_le_stabilizer_iota). So d.P upgrades to a KData d.G' (Subcomplex.ofIota d). A def InductionDatum.toKData : ... → KData ... making this explicit would let the induced-space reduction be stated as a corollary of the general reduction_to_qfd.
  • KData → InductionDatum (weakening direction). From any KData, one can form a corresponding InductionDatum by using ($K$-fix) to derive ($P$2) as a consequence — this would witness the fact that every K-cosheaf is also a P-cosheaf. However, this weakening is only useful if one then wants to induce $X = G \times^K X'$ from the K-cosheaf — a construction the paper does not perform in §2.7.

Both bridges are natural Lean-side follow-ups; the paper handles the $K \leftrightarrow P$ correspondence informally.

Hypotheses used

Statement Datum / instance hypotheses consumed
KData.K1b ($K$-fix) alone
orbit_iff_K IsQuasiFundDomain G' S + main compatibility hypothesis
qfd_equiv_hom IsQuasiFundDomain G' S + main compatibility hypothesis
ιOnSubcomplex_essSurj IsQuasiFundDomain G' S (surj)
ιOnSubcomplex_isEquivalence IsQuasiFundDomain G' S
funCatEquivOfQFD IsQuasiFundDomain G' S
GCosheaf.mapOfG_one GEquivariantCosheaf.act_one_inv (from the GEquivariant module)

The (P0)–(P2) fields of InductionDatum do not enter this node — the reduction is about QFDs, not about the induction construction. "Hypotheses" here means fields of KData, fields of IsQuasiFundDomain, and the main compatibility hypothesis carried as an explicit argument. None are Lean-kernel axiom declarations.

  /-- Underlying subgroup family. -/
  K : X → Subgroup G
  /-- **Cosheaf functoriality**: `E ≤ F → K_F ≤ K_E` (bigger cell has a

  K_mono : ∀ ⦃E F : X⦄, E ≤ F → K F ≤ K E
  /-- **G'-equivariance**: `K_{n·E} = n · K_E · n⁻¹` for `n ∈ G'`. -/
  K_equiv : ∀ (n : G') (E : X),
    K ((n : G) • E) = (K E).map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj (n : G)))
  /-- **Fixator dominance**: `K_E ≤ Fix_G(E) = Stab_G(E)`. -/
  K_le_fix : ∀ (E : X), K E ≤ MulAction.stabilizer G E

def endMorEquivStabilizer (E : OrbitCat G X) :
    Mor E E ≃ MulAction.stabilizer G (E : X) where
  toFun α := ⟨α.val, by
    show α.val • (E : X) = E
    by_contra h_ne
    have h_lt : AbstractCellComplex.dim (α.val • (E : X)) <
        AbstractCellComplex.dim (E : X) :=
      AbstractCellComplex.dim_lt α.property h_ne
    have h_eq : AbstractCellComplex.dim (α.val • (E : X)) =
        AbstractCellComplex.dim (E : X) :=
      GCellComplex.smul_dim α.val E
    omega⟩
  invFun k := ⟨k.val, by
    show k.val • (E : X) ≤ (E : X)
    rw [(k.property : k.val • (E : X) = E)]⟩
  left_inv _ := rfl
  right_inv _ := rfl
